holidays.name: National Junk Food Day
holidays.description: Today is a free pass to dive into the snack aisle. Think chips, candy bars, cheesy puffs and anything else that makes a nutritionist sigh. Skip the guilt and enjoy a crunchy, salty, sugary feast.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite on snack-lovers' calendars every July 21.
holidays.funFact: The phrase 'junk food' is often credited to Michael F. Jacobson of the Center for Science in the Public Interest, who used it in the early 1970s.

holidays.name: Invite an Alien to Live with You Day
holidays.description: Roll out the welcome mat for our friends from beyond the stars. Tidy the spare room, stock up on snacks, and perhaps leave a porch light on for any interstellar visitors. Just be sure to ask about their dietary needs first.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is a tongue-in-cheek nod to humanity's long fascination with extraterrestrial life and UFO lore.
holidays.funFact: The date lands in the same stretch of July as the anniversary of the 1947 Roswell incident, which helped launch America's modern UFO folklore.

holidays.name: National Tug-of-War Tournament Day
holidays.description: Grab a thick rope and pick a side. Today celebrates the sport where teamwork, grit and good footing beat everything else. Gather your friends, dig in your heels and heave.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It honors one of the oldest and simplest contests of strength.
holidays.funFact: Tug-of-war was an official Olympic event from 1900 to 1920.
